headline: Far-left party demands a ban on profit from welfare in budget talks
headline_short: Far-left party demands welfare profit ban
deck: The party calls it one of its priority demands; the prime minister promises nothing.
standard: Enhedslisten, a far-left party, will demand a ban on profit from publicly funded welfare in the coming budget negotiations. Private providers of supported housing, shelters, crisis centres and elderly care would have to run as self-governing institutions that reinvest any surplus.
Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, would not promise a ban but told Information she is 'not super keen' that money can be made 'from other people's misery'.

SF, a left-wing party, wants first to see whether a new rate model solves the problems. Radikale Venstre, a social-liberal party, accepts profit at crisis centres if it brings more places and better care.
short: Enhedslisten, a far-left party, will demand a ban on profit from publicly funded welfare, including crisis centres and elderly care, in the coming budget negotiations. Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, would not promise it.
